answer: To stem the tide of Sybil attacks in an agent economy, networks can mandate hardware-rooted attestation. Whether deployed across a coastal dune or an open meadow, each agent must sign transactions using a tamper-resistant secure enclave, imposing a verifiable hardware acquisition cost per identity. This blocks zero-cost virtual clones, though it cannot prevent well-funded adversaries from purchasing multiple physical chips or exploiting silicon side-channel flaws.
